svg.text: MAIN BOARD - power, true bypass, the input buffer, the Codec Zero's output
Part numbers match board-main.svg. A blue name is a net: the same name elsewhere - here, on another sheet, or a board's pad - is the same wire.
Centre negative, as every pedal: use a plastic-bodied
DC jack, or its +9 V sleeve touches the metal box.
True bypass, the input buffer, and the Codec Zero
bypass: the relay at rest - the guitar straight from INPUT to OUTPUT
INST (open): about 1 MΩ, unity gain - guitar and bass, passive or active.
LINE (closed): 6 dB quieter into the Codec Zero - synths, drum machines, keyboards.
The Codec Zero's own AUX IN gain (alsamixer) sets the level from there.
The relay, driven by the Pi
The Pi switches the effect in by driving BCM 25 high: Q1 energises K1,
which moves both contacts from NC to NO - the guitar through the buffer,
the Codec Zero and back out - and the ON LED lights.
BCM 25 rests low while the Pi boots, and R20 holds it low besides, so the
pedal is bypassed until the program is running, and if it ever stops.
The ON LED is lit by the relay's own current, so it always shows what the
relay is really doing. D2 takes the coil's kick when it lets go.
